task.title: Record HA and production deferred boundaries
task.shortdesc: State which production, HA, reverse-proxy, restore, and service-management capabilities are absent today and what can be prepared for later design work.

prereq.p: Readiness, network exposure, backup/export, monitoring, and update-window notes exist for the current source-run instance.

context.p: This topic records the boundary between current single-node source operation and future production architecture. It is deliberately explicit about what is planned but not implemented yet.

info.p: Write that BPM Administrator/DevOps documentation supports source deployment, manual configuration, health/readiness checks, API examples, manual backup evidence, documentation rebuild checks, and single-node update windows.

step.cmd: Name absent service and proxy capabilities.

info.p: List packaged services, native Linux service units, Windows services, official reverse-proxy recipes, TLS/proxy recipes, managed secrets, authentication gateway configuration, and production hardening as absent from BPM source documentation.

step.cmd: Name absent HA and upgrade capabilities.

info.p: List supported HA clustering, multi-node coordination, load balancer session affinity guidance, shared storage locking, zero-downtime migration, rolling upgrades, automatic failover, and official restore automation as future work, not current behavior.

step.cmd: Convert future needs into design inputs.

info.note: Do not place multiple source nodes behind a load balancer and call the result supported HA. Capture required RTO/RPO, backup verification, TLS ownership, secrets ownership, logging, monitoring, and upgrade-window expectations as inputs for later distribution/runtime tasks.

result.p: The boundary record prevents unsupported production, HA, and reverse-proxy claims while preserving useful preparation work for future releases.

postreq.p: Use this record during manual documentation QA and when future installer, service, reverse-proxy, and HA backlog items are approved.
